# Dynamic Ampacity Pipeline — Findings

**Generated by:** `code/05_dynamic_ampacity/run_all_stations.py`  
**Data:** USCRN multistation NPZ, 2019–2021 (3 years × 8,760 h = up to 26,280 h/station)  
**Cable:** Southwire 350 kcmil, EPR insulation, PVC jacket, PVC conduit (Southwire spec 46319 [V])  
**Neher-McGrath solver:** `code/01_cable_thermal_model/neher_mcgrath.py` [V Neher & McGrath 1957 / IEC 60287]  
**Johansen soil model:** `code/02_soil_thermal_properties/johansen.py` [V Johansen 1975]  
**Depth interpolation:** Crank-Nicolson solver, `code/04_depth_interpolation/depth_interp.py` [V Brunetti 2022]  
**Load factor:** 0.66 [V Bates 2021 Ch 9]  
**SCAN reference:** Ta=34.6°C, RHO=157 °C·cm/W (San Bernardino CA, Bates 2021 Ch 11) [V]

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **Station eligibility:** Only USCRN stations with valid soil sensors at **both 50 cm and 100 cm** depth are used (SM NaN rate < 50% at each). These depths bracket all standard cable burial depths (24"–36" = 0.61–0.91 m), enabling physical C-N interpolation. **72 of 131** multistation NPZ stations meet this criterion. Stations with only shallow sensors (5/10 cm — e.g. AZ Yuma, CO Boulder) are excluded: extrapolating from 10 cm to 76 cm is not physically valid.

## 1 Burial Depths Simulated [V NEC Table 300.5 / PG&E EDS 038193]

| Label | Depth | Application | Static Design Rating [R] |
|---|---|---|---|
| 24in | 0.610 m | NEC minimum, direct-buried conduit | **636 A** |
| 30in | 0.762 m | PG&E primary cable standard [V EDS 038193] | **621 A** |
| 36in | 0.914 m | Heavy-traffic / transmission routes | **610 A** |

Static rating computed with Black Books assumptions: RHO=90 °C·cm/W, Ta=20°C, LF=1.0, 3-cable trefoil, Southwire 350 kcmil [V Bates Table 3.1 / cable_params.py].

Deeper burial → slightly lower static rating (thicker soil column); difference 24"→36": **−26 A (−4%)** [R].

## 4 Key Findings

### 4.1 Real soil conditions are consistently better than NEC-90 design [R]

0% of station-hours across all 39 combinations fall below the static design rating. The NEC-90 Black Books worst-case (RHO=90, LF=1.0) is never the median real condition — actual soils are wetter and loads are less than continuous, yielding 85–145% headroom.

### 4.2 TX Monahans has lowest headroom: +83–87% at arid conditions [R]

TX Monahans (Permian Basin): mean RHO = 143.6 °C·cm/W at 30" — the driest station. Even so, dynamic ampacity (1153 A) is 85% above static (621 A). The SCAN worst-case (676 A) is the only scenario that approaches limiting conditions.

**This is the critical finding for PG&E's desert routes**: real capacity exists above static ratings, but arid zones have both the least headroom AND the most variability (std 9.5–11%), making soil moisture forecasting most valuable here.

### 4.3 CA stations relevant to PG&E's primary service territory [R]

- **CA Santa Barbara** (Mediterranean): 1430 A mean at 30", RHO=54.5 °C·cm/W, std only 1.9% — very stable wet coastal soil. Forecast value is low here (stable conditions); the headroom is large and predictable.
- **CA Bodega** (coastal): 1370 A, RHO=81.6, σ=2.4% — similar stability.

For PG&E's inland routes (Fresno, Bakersfield corridors), the NM/NV/TX arid stations are better analogues — high RHO, high variability, highest forecast value.

### 4.4 Depth effect: deeper burial modestly increases % headroom [R]

In most climate zones, headroom *increases* from 24" to 36" (by 3–8 pp) despite the lower static rating at 36". This occurs because deep soil temperature is more stable and slightly lower on average — thermal conditions at 91 cm are slightly better than at 61 cm. The exception is arid-SW where moisture uniformity with depth means the effect is minimal.

**Practical implication**: for new routes, 36" burial outperforms 24" not just mechanically (better protection) but thermally — a double benefit.

### 4.5 Headroom variability is the key metric for forecast value [R]

| Station | 30" σ (%) | Forecast value |
|---|---|---|
| NV_Mercury_3_SSW | 11.0% | **Highest** — Mojave swings critical |
| TX_Monahans_6_ENE | 9.5% | **High** — Permian Basin |
| AL_Fairhope_3_NE | 8.9% | High — subtropical monsoon |
| NM_Las_Cruces_20_N | 8.0% | High — Chihuahuan monsoon |
| NM_Socorro_20_N | 7.7% | Moderate-high |
| NE_Lincoln_8_ENE | 5.1% | Moderate |
| WY_Sundance_8_NNW | 4.5% | Moderate |
| OK_Stillwater_2_W | 3.8% | Moderate |
| OR_Riley_10_WSW | 2.8% | Low-moderate |
| NC_Asheville_13_S | 2.9% | Low-moderate |
| MI_Chatham_1_SE | 2.3% | Low |
| CA_Bodega_6_WSW | 2.4% | Low |
| CA_Santa_Barbara_11_W | 1.9% | **Lowest** — stable coastal |

σ = standard deviation of headroom_pct across 26,280 hourly observations. A 10% σ at 621 A static ≈ ±62 A inter-hour variation in available headroom — directly recoverable with a 24-hour soil moisture forecast.

### 4.6 Thermal resistivity at cable depth [R]

Mean RHO across all years at 30" burial:
- **Arid-SW**: 94–144 °C·cm/W — at or above NEC-90 assumption
- **Mediterranean**: 55–82 °C·cm/W — well below NEC-90
- **Sub-humid / Continental**: 54–77 °C·cm/W — consistently below NEC-90
- **Humid-subtropical**: 56–81 °C·cm/W — below NEC-90

Only arid zones match or exceed the design assumption. All others have significant latent capacity above what static ratings indicate.

---

## 5 Sensor & Interpolation Validation

**C-N solver NaN handling:** Stations with sensor outages (e.g. AL Fairhope ~4–14% NaN) are handled by forward-filling gaps before the C-N solve, then restoring NaN where *both* 50 cm and 100 cm sensors were simultaneously missing. The ffill introduces at most a few hours lag in estimated cable temperature — acceptable given the slow thermal time constant at 0.61–0.91 m depth.

**Moisture interpolation:** Linear between 50 cm and 100 cm sensors. Moisture gradients in this range are typically small and monotonic [V Wilson T1 data — clay content stable with depth at most stations]. Richards-equation coupling is a WP3 deliverable.
